resolutions.recorded_claim: The additional oral components caused a substantially higher burden for candidates.
resolutions.explanation: The original paragraph acknowledges that modularisation spread the examinations over time and made planning easier, then asserts a substantially greater burden from the oral components. The current rules corroborate the component structure; draft p. 15 estimates future direct oral minutes saved, while WPK describes reform proposals. Neither is a matched 2019 before/after assessment of the substantial causal burden asserted. Retain unresolved, without pretending that all dimensions must worsen to support it.
resolutions.limits: The author does not claim every candidate is worse off or all stress/workload measures rise. Additional assessment occasions plausibly impose organisational burden, while optional timing flexibility remains relevant to the stated substantial causal magnitude.

resolutions.recorded_claim: Nonfinancial developments often later have financial effects on the reporting company.
resolutions.explanation: In the original sustainability-assurance paragraph, this is an ordinary qualitative statement that nonfinancial developments commonly have later financial effects, not a numerical prevalence claim about every nonfinancial event. Independent EFRAG IG1 explicitly describes the dimensions as often intertwined, most material impacts developing financial risks/opportunities over time, and delayed cost/income mechanisms. The connectivity paper separately explains crystallisation in later reporting periods. This evidence supports the actual qualitative proposition; the prior demand for a measured universal frequency was stronger than its contextual wording.
resolutions.limits: Support is for the qualitative relationship in reporting, preserving often rather than replacing it with merely possible. Neither source supplies a statistical population frequency, ensures every event becomes financial, nor establishes audit-method identity or one-paper examination sufficiency. EFRAG IG1 is non-authoritative and scoped to ESRS/large CSRD reporting entities.

resolutions.recorded_claim: Credit continues to cease after material curriculum changes, preserving examination competence.
resolutions.explanation: Re-read law and October rationale confirm a continuing ability to refuse credit when curriculum changes destroy equivalence. But the full recorded compound also asserts cessation and preservation of competence. Current section 9(6) is a conditional refusal provision, not automatic cancellation after any material change; a fair reading makes materiality relative to equivalence. The exact September version remains unavailable, and the safeguard alone does not establish empirical unchanged competence. Retain unresolved rather than manufacture a wording error.
resolutions.limits: The author’s reasonable equivalence-related reading is retained. No error arises solely because the short phrase says credit ceases rather than spelling out the administrative refusal process.

new_evidence.check_result: Refusal can be justified where redesign removes equivalence.
Retains renumbered section 9(4) safeguard and states its quality rationale.
No dated September original recovered.

resolutions.resolution_blocker: Exact addressed text and the full safeguard/competence-effect compound are not independently settled.
resolutions.next_step: A recovered September text could settle its legal component; retain the separate scope of any quality-preservation inference instead of silently dropping it.

resolutions.recorded_claim: Working with professional pronouncements is standard audit practice.
resolutions.explanation: IDW p. 6 says work with professional pronouncements is standard in practice, then proposes their use as examination aids. It does not assert every publication is consulted in every assignment or that such use is a universal statutory duty. Independent BayObLG paragraphs 36–38 expressly recognise IDW pronouncements as accepted and commonly used, while distinguishing their lack of legal-norm status. Together with the professional examination catalogue this supports the ordinary standard-practice proposition. The prior survey demand across all assignments overstated the target.
resolutions.limits: The court’s case concerns valuation; it does not establish a measured profession-wide usage percentage, obligation to follow every IDW view, or that current examination aids already permit these publications. Those stronger propositions are not assessed as supported.

new_evidence.check_result: Independent judicial account expressly treats IDW pronouncements as accepted/common, without binding norm status.
Professional standards and business valuation are examined professional subject matter.

resolutions.next_step: Scheduled peer should independently re-read the court’s scope and the original open-book paragraph.

resolutions.recorded_claim: The addressed credit relief concerns university education and leaves advanced vocational qualifications outside its credit categories.
resolutions.explanation: BVBC’s 13 October letter does not identify a 23 September version. Its credit-scope description is directly corroborated by the ministry’s public October proposal, which predates that letter, and independently by WPO section 13b’s university-only statutory credit boundary. Article 2 supplies institutional higher-education relief, without a vocational-examination credit category. Requiring authentication of IDW’s separately named September dispatch was an inapplicable additional condition for this BVBC proposition.
resolutions.limits: No September dispatch bytes have been authenticated and no claim of their exact identity is made. Support applies to BVBC’s undated proposal reference and described features, not proof of delivery, enactment or achieved competence. Eight-year institutional confirmation differs from the existing individual degree-age limit.
